mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a given month leads to a short-term discounting effect that reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in similar tightening episodes are not statistically lower than in pre-tightening periods (two-tailed t-test, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2% in a month, it signals accelerating inflation expectations that compress real equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns during similar inflation spikes are not statistically worse than during stable inflation periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in monthly PAYEMS accompanied by a decline in UNRATE indicates strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: In regimes with similar labor indicators but no earnings momentum, 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (monthly index falling > -5%) suggests weakening manufacturing capacity, which reduces near-term demand for equities and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 5% in a month
failure_condition: During comparable supply shocks, 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST rises by at least 3% in a month, it reflects increased business inventory turnover and consumer demand strength, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥ 3% in a month
failure_condition: In analogous demand-recovery episodes, 5-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining GDPC1 (quarterly index) by more than 10% indicate deepening economic demand weakness, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by >10% in two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: During comparable multi-quarter demand contractions, 60-day forward returns are not significantly worse than in normal cycles (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RSAFS below 350,000 for three consecutive months suggests persistent excess saving and reduced consumption, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In similar excess-saving regimes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than in normal saving regimes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months while PAYEMS remains flat or increases, it signals a structural weakening of wage pressures and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for two consecutive months AND PAYEMS does not fall
failure_condition: In comparable labor-market transition episodes, 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during wage-stabilizing periods (p > 0.05).
